item.text:
**8B.7 Research Note: Fumio Kishida (2024)**

**Bottom line:** mixed, leaning negative. Kishida did get some indicators moving in the claimed direction, especially wages late in the year and post-disaster recovery spending, but the main household-welfare and trust indicators were still weak by year-end. The strongest positive signals were partial or lagged; the strongest negative signals were persistent real-wage weakness, cost-of-living pressure, and low approval.

- [Japan inflation-adjusted wages rise for two straight months in July](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/japan-inflationadjusted-wages-rise-for-two-straight-months-in-july-3601950) | Reuters | 2024-09-04 | Real wages rose 0.4% in July after a revised 1.1% gain in June, while nominal pay rose 3.6% and base pay posted its fastest increase in nearly 32 years. This is the clearest late-2024 sign that a key outcome Kishida wanted, higher wages, did move in the right direction, though bonuses helped and durability was not yet proven. | QIDs: 8B.7, 8B.6

- [Prime Minister Kishida briefing / reserve-fund recovery update](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202407/01kaiken.html) | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | 2024-07-01 | Kishida said the government had used more than 550 billion yen in reserve funds across multiple tranches to restore infrastructure, lifelines, housing, and livelihoods after the Noto earthquake. This is direct evidence that a claimed outcome, disaster recovery and livelihood restoration, was being pushed through state channels rather than left at the level of rhetoric. | QIDs: 8B.7, 8B.3, 8B.5

- [Japan downgrades view of economy on sluggish consumer spending](https://www.investing.com/news/economic-indicators/japan-downgrades-view-of-economy-on-sluggish-consumer-spending-3309375) | Reuters | 2024-02-21 | The government downgraded its economic view as real wages had fallen for 21 straight months and consumer spending remained weak. This is strong negative evidence that the hoped-for wage-and-demand turnaround was not yet happening in the inherited 2024 economy. | QIDs: 8B.7, 8B.6

- [Japan warns of weak yen impact on households in government white paper](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/japan-warns-of-weak-yen-impact-on-households-in-government-white-paper-3551065) | Reuters | 2024-08-01 | Japan’s own white paper said the weak yen was hurting household sentiment and purchasing power. That is a clear external-constraint signal: even with policy action, the household outcome Kishida sought was still being offset by currency and inflation pressure. | QIDs: 8B.7, 8B.6

- [Major August polls kept Kishida below 30% approval](https://www.nippon.com/en/japan-data/h30004/) | Nippon.com | 2024-08-30 | Jiji put Kishida at 19.4% approval and NHK at 25%, and respondents generally judged his decision to step down appropriate. If restoring trust in politics was the goal, the observable trust outcome did not move enough in the desired direction by late summer. | QIDs: 8B.7, 8B.6

- [Japan's Kishida championed 'new capitalism' but was undone by yen](https://www.thestar.com.my/news/world/2024/08/14/analysis-japan039s-kishida-championed-039new-capitalism039-but-was-undone-by-yen) | Reuters | 2024-08-14 | Reuters said Kishida had pushed some of Japan’s biggest wage increases in decades, but the weak yen, higher prices, and scandals outweighed that progress politically. This is the most balanced summary: some intended outcomes moved, but not far enough or fast enough to count as durable success. | QIDs: 8B.7, 8B.6

- [Liaison Meeting of the Government and Ruling Parties](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/actions/202407/03sei_yoto.html) | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | 2024-07-03 | Kishida reported that almost all bills and treaties had passed, including the Political Funds Control Act and child-care support legislation. This is an intermediate implementation result, not a final social outcome, but it does show declarations turning into observable state action. | QIDs: 8B.7, 8B.3, 8B.5

**Search gap:** I found strong 2024 evidence for wages, consumer purchasing power, approval/trust, and disaster recovery. I did not find equally solid 2024 quantitative outcome series for child-support effects, regional revitalization, or nuclear-disarmament diplomacy. For those areas, the available evidence is mostly process/output reporting rather than hard outcome measurement.
